result.reason: This lens audits contract completeness, containment, owner default-entry, transition-group guard collisions, and wrong local-exit targets by contrasting the exact source inventory/canonical IR against the closed FCSTM. Key findings: (1) HumanDrivingMode and AutonomousMode are declared composite in source but simple/composite in FCSTM consistent with NL1/NL2 (satisfied, omitted). (2) NL3's root->HumanDrivingMode initial edge exists at transition:line:19 but that pseudostate edge carries a trigger (Power_On) and is flagged INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL/refuted by verify_facts, and is unreachable per event-consumer facts, so the exact power-on-triggered initial entry into HumanDrivingMode is not an unconditional default entry -- this is the same NL3-INIT-1 obligation, already covered by contract NL-CONTRACT-NL3-INIT-1, and separately the root composite itself lacks any unconditional entry (reference_inspection_facts W_INITIAL_UNCONDITIONAL_MISSING) supporting the derived owner-entry issue. (3) NL4 endpoint HumanDrivingMode->AutonomousMode exists (transition:line:20) with trigger front_distance_10 but the closed model expresses this as a trigger/event, not a guard field (guard=null) -- contract NL4-GUARD-1 requires guard=front_distance>10 equal, but transition has no guard field; the frozen S5 guard predicate cannot be satisfied by a trigger-only transition since the model encodes it as an event. This is a wrong_guard mismatch: expected value is a guard, observed is empty guard field (value moved to trigger). (4) NL4.2 endpoint AutonomousMode->HumanDrivingMode exists via macro transition:line:18, but the trigger set required (human steering cmd + brake pressed OR in AutoFinal) is realized quite differently: the actual model splits this into two internal region-exit transitions (AutoNavigating->[*] and AutoFinal->[*] both triggered by Human_Steering_Cmd_Brake_Pressed_in_AutoFinal effect setting R45RouteToken=5) plus one outer guarded transition AutonomousMode->HumanDrivingMode guarded by R45RouteToken==5 with no triggers of its own. This structural decomposition means the exact triggerable condition described in NL (three distinct alternatives: steering cmd, brake pressed, in-AutoFinal) is collapsed into a single compiled event name and a route-token guard, which is contrastively inconsistent with the required trigger_set as three independent named alternatives -- however per macro-boundary rules, this is one macro/compiled construct grounded via source_trace to tr_0005, so it may satisfy as a compiled whole; nonetheless the AutoFinal state referenced in the guard 'in (auto final)' is realized as an exit-only state (no outgoing edge other than exit), consistent NL4.2-CONTAIN-1 (AutoFinal contained in AutonomousMode) is satisfied structurally (state:AutoFinal:line:11, parent AutonomousMode). (5) NL5 endpoint root->FinalState exists (transition:line:21) but is INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL/refuted (has trigger Power_Off, unreachable per event-consumer fact), and FinalState itself is a LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING deadlock leaf per both inspection_equivalent_facts and reference_inspection_facts -- this directly supports NL5-TERM-1 termination concerns from a structural-contrast angle (the terminal edge is unreachable, so the state can never be reached to terminate, which is itself a structural entry defect on the same root scope that also affects NL3). (6) A derived containment observation: exact_source_inventory/canonical IR shows AutonomousMode composite has exactly two direct children (AutoNavigating, AutoFinal) confirming NL2-DERIVED containment is satisfied. (7) Structural contrast surfaces one new issue not captured by existing contracts: the root composite (llms_emp_feedback_final_0000) has TWO competing initial pseudostate edges into two different targets (HumanDrivingMode via Power_On-triggered edge, FinalState via Power_Off-triggered edge) and NEITHER is unconditional/default, per reference_inspection_facts W_INITIAL_UNCONDITIONAL_MISSING naming HumanDrivingMode as suggested first-child fallback. This is a structural owner-default-entry gap on the root scope distinct from the specific NL3 wording, since NL3 only asks for a power-on-triggered entry (which nominally exists as an edge) while the deeper structural defect is that the owning root composite has no unconditional/reachable default initial edge at all, making both conditional initial edges (line 19, line 21) permanently unreachable/refuted. I derive one additional_contracts row for this owner-level default-entry gap grounded in NL3's segment (the only NL segment discussing root-level initial behavior) since the existing NL3-INIT-1 contract is narrower (only checks existence of an edge to HumanDrivingMode), not the owner's structural unconditional-entry defect that makes it unreachable.

the endpoint-existence alternative addresses a different (weaker) property per the property-preservation protocol, so it does not rebut, but remains a competent undercutting reading about which typed property S2 endpoint-existence checks, hence undercutting-survives. i5 (Power_Off transition endpoint) parallels i3 with the same disposition. i6 (FinalState termination stability) is established from LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING plus refuted initial-entry; the "state itself represents termination" defense is a different property (structural leaf vs. reachable stable termination) and does not rebut per protocol, but remains undercutting since two properties are compatible with the same facts, so undercutting-survives. i7 (event consumer coverage) is established because verify_facts explicitly refutes event-consumer:Power_Off reachability; the declared-consumer defense addresses a weaker property (declaration only) and per the property-preservation protocol a declared-but-unreachable consumer does not rebut a reachable-consumer requirement, so the defeater is defeated and the reading stands as a violation with no competent alternative for the exact required property (defeater_kind=none since the only proposed defense is not competent under the protocol's explicit declared-consumer clause). i10 (V1 deadlock/dead-end at FinalState) is established: the exact model shows FinalState is reachable, non-final (explicit_final=false), with zero outgoing transitions and no inherited continuation; the V1 backend execution failed to reach a Boolean verdict (worker_did_not_exit), which is a W boundary, not evidence against the semantic finding; no exact terminal edge or terminal fact is supplied, so the intentional-terminal alternative does not survive (defeated) per the V1 frontier protocol. i12 (two initial edges same region) is established from PlantUML lines 2 and 14 showing two [*] edges in the same region, contradicted only by UML's own rule about at most one initial edge — the "closed model is internally consistent" defense does not resolve the source-level double-declaration defect, so this stands with an undercutting alternative (declaration-order resolution) surviving since the exact registry lacks a dedicated predicate and two readings (defect vs. tie-broken-by-order) remain compatible. i13 and i14 are frontier-unresolved containment checks explicitly marked binding_status=identity_unresolved with no model refs; per protocol these are genuinely undecidable from the dossier, so grounding=unresolved. i15 and i16 are exactly-bound S3 trigger-set-equals checks on the initial pseudostate transitions; the backend receipt shows the required trigger set is empty (per UML invariant) but the actual native transitions carry Power_On / Power_Off triggers respectively, giving verdict=false with an exact counterexample; the strongest rebuttal offered (only the exact carrier is evaluated) does not rebut but confirms the violation, and no competent alternative reading is available since the invariant is a frozen domain rule inherently applicable to any transition originating from an initial pseudostate, so defeater_kind=none, disposition=defeated for i15/i16.

issues.reason: S2 covers exact endpoint existence, but the deterministic verify_facts explicitly refutes this specific initial-entry check as non-reachable/conditional, which is the disqualifying condition documented in the frozen-predicate routing discipline for initial-entry facts with conditional guards/triggers on pseudostate edges.
issues.requirement_quote: when power on, the system turn into human driving mode
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The edge does exist syntactically and targets the correct state HumanDrivingMode with the correct Power_On trigger; if the registry's S2 predicate only checks endpoint existence irrespective of the reachable_from_initial flag, this could be read as satisfied at the endpoint layer, leaving only a coverage-layer defect.
issues.title: Power-on initial entry edge into HumanDrivingMode carries a conditional trigger and is not reachable from the top-level initial state

issues.basis: verify_facts.checks initial-entry:transition:line:19 refuted; inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions line 19 reachable_from_initial=false; diagnostics INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL.
issues.expected: The power-on event must deterministically and reachably drive the system into HumanDrivingMode from the actual top-level initial pseudostate of the machine.
issues.observed: The only power-on entry (transition:line:19) is conditional/triggered and inspection_equivalent_facts records reachable_from_initial=false for it; verify_facts refutes initial-entry:transition:line:19. There is no unconditional fallback initial edge at the root scope (confirmed by reference_inspection_facts W_INITIAL_UNCONDITIONAL_MISSING).
issues.reason: This is a behavioral-consequence obligation distinct from the bare initial_entry declaration property: NL3 requires the power-on stimulus to actually cause entry, and the deterministic facts show the sole such edge is refuted as a reachable unconditional initial-entry, which is a genuine root reachability gap for the power-on response even though the state ref itself is marked reachable in aggregate closure metrics.
issues.requirement_quote: when power on, the system turn into human driving mode
issues.strongest_rebuttal: HumanDrivingMode itself appears in reachable_state_refs and reachability.[*] list with reachable_from_initial=true at the state level, suggesting the state is reachable through some closure path even if this specific edge is flagged conditional, which could rebut a strict unreachable claim.
issues.title: Power-on response path into HumanDrivingMode is not established as reachable from the machine's true top-level initial entry

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions transition:line:21 (reachable_from_initial=false, triggers=[Power_Off]); diagnostics INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL line 21; verify_facts.checks initial-entry:transition:line:21 refuted.
issues.expected: A transition from the current/enclosing operating scope to FinalState on power-off that is actually usable during system operation.
issues.observed: The only edge to FinalState is [*] -> FinalState (transition:line:21), triggered by Power_Off, flagged INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL, with reachable_from_initial=false in inspection_equivalent_facts, and verify_facts refutes initial-entry:transition:line:21.
issues.reason: The endpoint exists but is a second, competing top-level initial edge alongside the Power_On edge, and the deterministic facts show it is not reachable as a genuine operational transition from the enclosing operating scope; this is the negative behavioral fact under the endpoint-existence property.
issues.requirement_quote: when power off, it will transit to final state
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The edge exists with correct source (an initial pseudostate scoped at root) and correct target FinalState and correct Power_Off trigger, which may be read as satisfying bare S2 endpoint existence regardless of the reachable_from_initial flag.
issues.title: Power-off transition to FinalState exists only as a conditional/unreachable initial pseudostate edge

issues.basis: diagnostics LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING line 17; reference_inspection_facts W_DEADLOCK_LEAF; inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions line 21 reachable_from_initial=false; verify_facts.checks deadlock:state:FinalState:line:17 refuted and initial-entry:transition:line:21 refuted.
issues.expected: The final state reached on power off must represent a stable, reachable completion of the system's operation.
issues.observed: FinalState (state:FinalState:line:17) has outgoing_transition_refs=[] (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING diagnostic, reference_inspection_facts W_DEADLOCK_LEAF) and its sole entry is transition:line:21, an initial pseudostate edge marked reachable_from_initial=false and refuted by verify_facts as a genuine initial-entry. Thus the completion path required by NL5 is not established as an operationally reachable, stable termination route.
issues.reason: Per the termination-contract audit discipline, this lens must inspect target and active-ancestor continuation as well as whether the designated ending path is genuinely operationally reachable; the combination of an unreachable/conditional sole entry edge and a leaf-without-outgoing diagnostic together show the power-off completion path is not stably established as required.
issues.requirement_quote: when power off, it will transit to final state
issues.strongest_rebuttal: Global reachability metrics list FinalState in reachable_state_refs with reachable_from_initial=true at the aggregate closure level, and it does have zero outgoing transitions consistent with a terminal design; one could argue the state itself correctly represents termination once reached, independent of the entry-edge reachability defect.
issues.title: FinalState is a reachable leaf with no outgoing transition, but its only entry edge is an unreachable conditional initial edge, undermining stable termination semantics

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers Power_Off row; diagnostics EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE Power_Off; verify_facts.checks event-consumer:Power_Off refuted.
issues.expected: The power-off event must have at least one reachable consumer transition realizing the transit-to-final-state response during actual system operation.
issues.observed: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers for Power_Off lists consumer_transition_refs=[transition:line:21] but reachable_consumer_state_refs=[] and reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]; diagnostics record EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE for Power_Off; verify_facts.checks event-consumer:Power_Off is refuted.
issues.reason: Declaration-only presence of a consumer transition does not discharge the stronger reachable-consumer-coverage property required for an operational power-off response; the deterministic event-consumer facts and verify_facts explicitly refute reachability of this consumer, matching the frozen routing guidance to keep declaration and operational coverage as distinct properties.
issues.requirement_quote: when power off, it will transit to final state
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The event is declared and syntactically wired to a transition targeting FinalState, so a reviewer might argue the declaration itself satisfies the NL's operational intent even though deterministic reachability flags it as unreachable.
issues.title: Power_Off event has a declared consumer transition but no reachable consumer from the top-level initial entry

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions transition:line:18 (triggers=[], guard='R45RouteToken == 5'); transition:line:14 and transition:line:15 carry triggers=[Human_Steering_Cmd_Brake_Pressed_in_AutoFinal] with effects R45RouteToken=5, distinct from transition:line:18.
issues.expected: The AutonomousMode-to-HumanDrivingMode transition must be triggerable by receiving a human steering command, brake pressed, or being in the auto-final sub-state, i.e. it should carry the composite Human_Steering_Cmd_Brake_Pressed_in_AutoFinal event/trigger (as declared in the FCSTM event list) or an equivalent explicit trigger/guard reflecting those three conditions.
issues.observed: The actual closed-model transition (transition:line:18, AutonomousMode -> HumanDrivingMode) has triggers=[] and guard='R45RouteToken == 5' with effect R45RouteToken=0; the required Human_Steering_Cmd_Brake_Pressed_in_AutoFinal event is instead consumed only by the internal AutoNavigating/AutoFinal -> [*] exit transitions (transition:line:14, transition:line:15) which set R45RouteToken=5 as a side channel, not by the AutonomousMode->HumanDrivingMode transition itself.
issues.reason: The contract requires this exact transition's trigger set to equal the three-way event; the deterministic transition-fact data shows this transition carries no triggers at all and only a distinct internal-variable guard, which is a mismatched trigger_set on the exact carrier transition even though a related internal relay mechanism exists elsewhere in the model.
issues.requirement_quote: transit to human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final)
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The overall behavioral effect could be considered equivalent: firing Human_Steering_Cmd_Brake_Pressed_in_AutoFinal inside AutonomousMode sets R45RouteToken=5, causing the guarded AutonomousMode->HumanDrivingMode transition to become enabled, so the composite mechanism might functionally realize the same trigger/guard semantics as required, even though it is expressed as a route-token relay rather than a directly-attached trigger set.
issues.title: AutonomousMode-to-HumanDrivingMode transition uses an internal route-token guard instead of the three required NL triggers/condition

branches.reason: This lens audits contract completeness, containment, owner default-entry, transition-group guard collisions, and wrong local-exit targets by contrasting the exact source inventory/canonical IR against the closed FCSTM. Key findings: (1) HumanDrivingMode and AutonomousMode are declared composite in source but simple/composite in FCSTM consistent with NL1/NL2 (satisfied, omitted). (2) NL3's root->HumanDrivingMode initial edge exists at transition:line:19 but that pseudostate edge carries a trigger (Power_On) and is flagged INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL/refuted by verify_facts, and is unreachable per event-consumer facts, so the exact power-on-triggered initial entry into HumanDrivingMode is not an unconditional default entry -- this is the same NL3-INIT-1 obligation, already covered by contract NL-CONTRACT-NL3-INIT-1, and separately the root composite itself lacks any unconditional entry (reference_inspection_facts W_INITIAL_UNCONDITIONAL_MISSING) supporting the derived owner-entry issue. (3) NL4 endpoint HumanDrivingMode->AutonomousMode exists (transition:line:20) with trigger front_distance_10 but the closed model expresses this as a trigger/event, not a guard field (guard=null) -- contract NL4-GUARD-1 requires guard=front_distance>10 equal, but transition has no guard field; the frozen S5 guard predicate cannot be satisfied by a trigger-only transition since the model encodes it as an event. This is a wrong_guard mismatch: expected value is a guard, observed is empty guard field (value moved to trigger). (4) NL4.2 endpoint AutonomousMode->HumanDrivingMode exists via macro transition:line:18, but the trigger set required (human steering cmd + brake pressed OR in AutoFinal) is realized quite differently: the actual model splits this into two internal region-exit transitions (AutoNavigating->[*] and AutoFinal->[*] both triggered by Human_Steering_Cmd_Brake_Pressed_in_AutoFinal effect setting R45RouteToken=5) plus one outer guarded transition AutonomousMode->HumanDrivingMode guarded by R45RouteToken==5 with no triggers of its own. This structural decomposition means the exact triggerable condition described in NL (three distinct alternatives: steering cmd, brake pressed, in-AutoFinal) is collapsed into a single compiled event name and a route-token guard, which is contrastively inconsistent with the required trigger_set as three independent named alternatives -- however per macro-boundary rules, this is one macro/compiled construct grounded via source_trace to tr_0005, so it may satisfy as a compiled whole; nonetheless the AutoFinal state referenced in the guard 'in (auto final)' is realized as an exit-only state (no outgoing edge other than exit), consistent NL4.2-CONTAIN-1 (AutoFinal contained in AutonomousMode) is satisfied structurally (state:AutoFinal:line:11, parent AutonomousMode). (5) NL5 endpoint root->FinalState exists (transition:line:21) but is INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL/refuted (has trigger Power_Off, unreachable per event-consumer fact), and FinalState itself is a LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING deadlock leaf per both inspection_equivalent_facts and reference_inspection_facts -- this directly supports NL5-TERM-1 termination concerns from a structural-contrast angle (the terminal edge is unreachable, so the state can never be reached to terminate, which is itself a structural entry defect on the same root scope that also affects NL3). (6) A derived containment observation: exact_source_inventory/canonical IR shows AutonomousMode composite has exactly two direct children (AutoNavigating, AutoFinal) confirming NL2-DERIVED containment is satisfied. (7) Structural contrast surfaces one new issue not captured by existing contracts: the root composite (llms_emp_feedback_final_0000) has TWO competing initial pseudostate edges into two different targets (HumanDrivingMode via Power_On-triggered edge, FinalState via Power_Off-triggered edge) and NEITHER is unconditional/default, per reference_inspection_facts W_INITIAL_UNCONDITIONAL_MISSING naming HumanDrivingMode as suggested first-child fallback. This is a structural owner-default-entry gap on the root scope distinct from the specific NL3 wording, since NL3 only asks for a power-on-triggered entry (which nominally exists as an edge) while the deeper structural defect is that the owning root composite has no unconditional/reachable default initial edge at all, making both conditional initial edges (line 19, line 21) permanently unreachable/refuted. I derive one additional_contracts row for this owner-level default-entry gap grounded in NL3's segment (the only NL segment discussing root-level initial behavior) since the existing NL3-INIT-1 contract is narrower (only checks existence of an edge to HumanDrivingMode), not the owner's structural unconditional-entry defect that makes it unreachable.
